newsitem.title: SPAIN: Better H2 boosts Repsol 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Better H2 boosts Repsol 1996 net profit.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol said on Wednesday its 1996 net attributable profit nudged up 1.1 percent to 119.01 billion pesetas, helped by an improvement in its performance in the second half of the year.
Operating profit however fell to 197.23 billion pesetas from 212.50 billion. Extraordinary losses fell to 1.11 billion from losses of 7.04 billion pesetas in 1995.

"The favourable performance in the second half (of the year) has allowed the company to obtain the best results in its history," the company said in a note. A full breakdown of results would be made available later, a spokesman said.
At 1300 GMT, Repsol was down 110 pesetas, or 1.90 percent, to 5,670, underperforming the Ibex-35 index of leading shares which was down 1.85 percent at 5,255.85.
"The net profit figure is slightly better than expected, probably due to financial results," said a dealer at Central Hispano Bolsa brokerage.
Financial losses narrowed to 8.23 billion pesetas from 16.57 billion pesetas in 1996. Tax payments also improved, falling to 55.55 billion pesetas from 60.56 billion a year earlier.

In the nine months to September, Repsol posted a 5.6 percent fall in net profit to 86.98 billion pesetas. The firm said the chemical division was the only one which did not improve its operating results.
Some analysts have predicted a recovery in chemicals in the fourth quarter, as well as greater contributions from Repsol's exploration and production divisions.

The operating profit is not directly comparable to the previous year's figures because income will have been boosted by the purchase of a 37.7 percent controlling stake in Argentine refinery Astra as well as Repsol's inclusion in a consortium which bought 60 percent of Peru's la Pampilla refinery in the second quarter of 1996.
The Spanish government is due to sell its remaining 10 percent stake in the firm on the stock market later this year.
